title: Verdict and Will
premise: When a drowned man washes up on the tidal flats outside Saltmere Bay wearing Theo Brightwater's own stolen clothes, the police assume a case of mistaken identity — until the dental records name him as Daniel Voss, the key witness in an upcoming corruption trial who everyone, including his grieving sister, swears died three years ago. Theo, whose quiet pattern-reading has already unmasked three 'accidents,' realizes the body is a message aimed at her: someone knows what she is and wants her silenced or discredited. As she traces the witness's double life — two identities, two women who loved him, and a ledger hidden beneath the pier — Theo discovers the 'dead' man may still be alive, hiding in the one place no one looks. In the end, loyalty to the sister who lied to protect him collides with Theo's need for truth, and at low tide Theo must choose whether to expose a living witness whose testimony will destroy the town's beloved benefactor — or let the sea keep its secret.
about_author: Lior Halloran is a former night-desk clerk at a coastal grand hotel who spent a decade listening to guests lie beautifully. Verdict and Will is the fourth novel in the acclaimed Brightwater mysteries, praised for its quiet observation and tide-turning tension.

chapters.title: The Man in My Coat
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A body washes up at dawn wearing Theo's monogrammed overcoat, and the police — who owe her a grudging respect — ask her to confirm the clothing is hers. She recognizes the stitching, the moth hole, the theft from her own closet. Emotional beat: violated intimacy; the hunter has become the marked.

chapters.title: A Dead Man with a Pulse in His File
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The corpse is identified as Daniel Voss — declared dead three years ago and the star witness in the Harrow trial. Theo pulls his old file and finds contradictions: a death certificate signed by a doctor who left town, and a hotel register she remembers falsifying herself, years ago, for a man who paid in cash. Beat: the past was never closed.

chapters.title: What the Sister Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, with a brief flashback to Voss's. She interviews Maren Voss, the witness's sister, whose grief rings rehearsed — until Theo notices fresh flowers on a grave that never holds any. Maren warns her off with a loyalty that sounds like fear. Beat: Theo recognizes a lie told out of love, because she has told them herself.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Hand
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Revisiting her three solved 'accidents,' Theo finds they all connect to Harrow's shipping empire and to the same missing ledger. Someone in town is cleaning house before the trial, and the drowned man in her coat was meant to be a warning shot. Beat: dread hardens into purpose.

chapters.title: The Second Identity
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Theo investigating, and an unnamed man watching her from the pier. Theo traces Voss's double life — a rented room under the name 'Will Merrow,' a second woman, Corinne, who believes her partner is a lighthouse keeper. Beat: identity as a kindness and a cage; Theo begins to suspect the dead man breathes.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At an extreme low tide, the sea exposes a rusted strongbox beneath the old pier — the ledger — but someone reaches it first, leaving only a torn page and boot prints she recognizes from her own closet. Beat: the hunter is inside the house; Theo realizes she was never the target, only the messenger.

chapters.title: Corinne's Tide Chart
chapters.summary: Corinne's POV. Corinne, piecing together her partner's absences, confronts Theo, and the two women trade what they know: he is alive, he is hiding, and he is running out of places to run. Beat: rivalry dissolves into alliance; two keepers of the same secret finally meet.

chapters.title: The Benefactor's Smile
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She confronts Aldous Harrow at his charity gala, laying out the pattern of deaths with the calm of a concierge reading a guest's lie. Harrow's composure cracks by a millimeter — enough. That night her hotel room is searched and a threatening note is left folded like a turndown card. Beat: open war.

chapters.title: What the Sea Took Back
chapters.summary: Climax. Storm tide. Theo, Maren, and Corinne converge on the lighthouse where Daniel Voss has been hiding; Harrow's fixer follows them. Voss must choose between lifelong silence and testimony; Maren must choose between her brother and the truth she buried. The fixer attacks; Voss saves Theo, revealing himself at last. Beat: truth dragged into the light by force of love.

chapters.title: Verdict and Will
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. Voss testifies; Harrow falls; Maren faces charges for faking the death and accepts them without regret. Corinne and Voss leave town together, strangers to their old names. Theo returns the overcoat to her closet, mended. Beat: loyalty and truth reconciled at cost; the tide keeps only what it is given.
